handbookNote: Maryland has no single official state-administered boating knowledge exam; boaters satisfy the state's mandatory boater education law by completing a Maryland DNR-approved, NASBLA-aligned course (e.g., Boat-Ed/Kalkomey), whose own embedded final exam serves as the qualifying test -- Boat-Ed's Maryland course independently confirms an 80% minimum passing score on the final exam with unlimited retake attempts, and a typical completion time of 3-4 hours (this 80%/unlimited-attempts convergence matches this project's WA/AZ/MA boating precedent) -- Maryland's mandate itself is a genuine, currently active law confirmed independently by two sources (boat-ed.com Maryland and the BoatUS Foundation's Maryland state boating law summary): anyone born on or after July 1, 1972 must carry a certificate of boating safety education while operating a numbered or documented (motorized) vessel on Maryland waters, with a stricter absolute rule that no one under 16 may ever operate a personal watercraft even with a certificate, while an under-16 operator of a larger motorized vessel (11 ft+) without a certificate may operate under supervision of a certified adult at least 18; exemptions include out-of-state visitors (<=60 days), foreign vessel operators (<=90 days), private-property-only operation, and certain commercial operation -- content is also grounded in the Maryland Natural Resources Article (Md. Code Ann., Nat. Res.), including vessel numbering and titling (Sec. 8-712, 8-716), hull identification numbers (Sec. 8-711), vessel abandonment (Sec. 8-722, 8-725.2), water-skiing/towing rules (Sec. 8-725), littering (Sec. 8-726), boating-under-the-influence and post-accident impairment testing (Sec. 8-738, 8-738.1), and reckless operation and escalating-penalty provisions (Sec. 8-738.2, 8-738.3), each independently verified against the Maryland General Assembly's own statute-text database (mgaleg.maryland.gov) -- plus universal NASBLA-aligned boating-safety fundamentals (PFDs, required equipment, Navigation Rules, aids to navigation, cold-water immersion, and weather) and Chesapeake Bay-specific content (commercial shipping traffic in dredged channels, crab-pot/trotline navigation hazards, tidal vs. non-tidal waters, and Natural Resources Police statewide enforcement authority) drawn from Maryland DNR/NRP public boating-safety messaging (dnr.maryland.gov); federal boating-accident-reporting deadlines (48 hours for death/serious injury, 10 days for property damage/lesser injury) are presented as the general baseline since a Maryland-specific deviation from that federal threshold was not independently re-verified against the exact state statute in this build -- price matches this project's Motorcycle-tier boating convention ($7.99), not a placeholder
